ety.text: From социали́зм (socialízm) + шовини́зм (šovinízm). The concept of social chauvinism as a kind of opportunism was first used by Vladimir Ulyanov-Lenin in the pamphlet Dead Chauvinism and Living Socialism (1914).
Ultimately from Latin phoenīx (likely via a Western European language; cf. French phénix), itself from Ancient Greek φοῖνιξ (phoînix).
